The Long Read

On maps and territories

Every model of the world leaves something out. The question is what.

A map that showed everything would be as large as the land itself, and just as hard to read. Usefulness comes from leaving things out.

Engineers know this well. A good diagram hides the details that do not matter for the question at hand.

The art of the model is choosing what to ignore.

Problems begin when we forget that the map was a choice. We start to treat the simplified picture as if it were the real thing.

When the map is wrong

Old sea charts sometimes showed islands that did not exist. Sailors searched for them for decades.

The error was not in drawing an island that turned out to be imaginary. It was in never checking.

Keeping models honest

Write down the assumptions next to the model. Revisit them when the results surprise you.

And when someone shows you a perfectly clean chart, ask what was left out to make it so clean.

The author writes about systems, uncertainty, and the stories numbers tell.
